customer_question: Besides incorporating the certification test tool, does our product software need any behavior-restricting modification for profile testing? Specifically, can AVRCP be tested when our product always connects it together with A2DP rather than advertising it independently?
question_variants: Will PTS be able to test a profile our product never independently advertises?
Do we need special test-only firmware for AVRCP if it's bundled with A2DP?
How can we check beforehand whether a profile will be testable?
actual_issue: The customer's automotive infotainment product implemented AVRCP so that it always connects together with A2DP, advertising only A2DP at Inquiry time rather than independently advertising AVRCP, raising the question of whether PTS could still test AVRCP as required, and whether any product software modification was needed for testing beyond the standard certification tool.
plain_english_explanation: Before a Bluetooth test tool can test a specific feature of a device, that feature needs to show up on its own in the device's list of advertised capabilities when another device looks for it. Some car infotainment products are built so that one feature (like music-playback controls) always tags along automatically with another (like audio streaming) instead of being separately announced -- which works fine for real-world use, but means the test tool can't isolate and test that tagging-along feature on its own. In that situation, a special test-only version of the software that lets the feature be found and connected independently is needed, and it's worth checking for this kind of issue ahead of time using an ordinary phone's Bluetooth app, rather than discovering it mid-test.
consultant_answer: In principle, profile testing is performed using the product's own embedded software as-is, with no modification needed beyond the standard certification test tool. However, past experience shows that a profile not announced in the device's SDP record at the initial Inquiry cannot be tested. For example, in car infotainment products where AVRCP is always used together with A2DP, with the implementation advertising only A2DP at Inquiry (and AVRCP connecting alongside it automatically), PTS cannot test AVRCP as a standalone connection, since AVRCP isn't independently inquirable -- in such cases, test-only modified software allowing AVRCP to be independently inquired and connected has had to be provided in the past. Since the test lab cannot know this in advance without actually running PTS, the customer should pre-check beforehand by using a smartphone's Bluetooth app to display the target device's list of supported profiles, confirming whether every profile intended for testing actually appears as independently visible.
decision_logic: A profile that is not independently advertised in a product's SDP record at Inquiry time -- because the implementation bundles its connection with another profile's -- cannot be tested by PTS as a standalone item unless test-only modified software is provided that makes it independently inquirable and connectable; this should be verified before submission via a smartphone Bluetooth app rather than discovered only once PTS testing begins.
final_recommendation: Before submitting a product for profile testing, especially for automotive or similarly bundled-implementation products, have the customer check via a smartphone Bluetooth app whether every profile intended for testing is independently visible in the device's advertised SDP record; if a profile is bundled with another and not independently advertised, arrange for test-only modified software that makes it independently testable.
risk_if_done_wrong: Submitting a product for profile testing without this pre-check risks discovering only during PTS testing that a bundled profile cannot be tested as a standalone item, requiring last-minute modified test software and delaying the test schedule.
